newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong overnight rates close off highs.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong overnight rates close off highs.

text.p: Overnight rates in Hong Kong closed off their highs on Tuesday after an unsettled day's trading in which they soared near 20 percent on currency fears.

Traders said banks were reacting to a warning from the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), Hong Kong's de facto central bank, that some banks betting against the Hong Kong dollar might be charged more for money.
"People went to square their (Hong Kong dollar) positions," a dealer said.
HKMA chief Joseph Yam said on Sunday that speculators would be punished with crippling rates.
"Those banks involved in the speculation will suffer by paying a high interest rate to get the Hong Kong dollar funding to settle the deals," Yam told the South China Morning Post.
Overnight rates soared to 18.00/20.00 percent early on Tuesday as a result of the warning before edging down to 10.00/12.00 percent, dealers said.

Dealers said there was no overt sign that the HKMA had intervened in the market, although they said that there were unconfirmed rumours that the authority may have lent short-term money at high rates.
Despite the day's volatility, dealers said volumes were thin, and the Hong Kong dollar was relatively stable, also in thin trade.
The Hong Kong dollar is the last major currency in Asia that is pegged to the U.S. dollar, and has been sold off recently on nervousness that speculators might seek to break the peg.
Hong Kong's chief executive Tung Chee-hwa warned on Tuesday that speculators attacking the Hong Kong dollar were "bound to fail."
Dealers said the market was waiting to see the outcome of a meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), the U.S. central bank's policy-making group, to be held during U.S. hours on Tuesday.
By the close on Tuesday, overnight rates were between eight percent and 10 percent, depending on the quoted bank.
Late on Tuesday, the Hong Kong dollar was quoted at 7.7385/95, mildly firmer than an opening level of HK$7.400/10 and off the day's lows of HK$7.425/35.
